## Oncology and Cancer Care

### Advanced Oncology & Cancer Care for Pets in Las Vegas

At West Flamingo Animal Hospital, we know that a cancer diagnosis can be overwhelming. That’s why we’re proud to offer specialized veterinary oncology services—providing hope, expertise, and compassionate care for pets and their families throughout Las Vegas. With advanced diagnostics and treatment options, we’re here to guide you every step of the way in your pet’s fight against cancer.

Image

Image

### Meet Our Expert: Dr. Dennis Macy

Our oncology services are led by one of the most respected names in veterinary medicine—Dennis Macy, DVM, MS, Diplomate ACVIM. Recognized as one of the top veterinary oncologists in the world, Dr. Macy brings decades of experience and cutting-edge knowledge to every case. When he’s not seeing patients at our Las Vegas location or in Palm Springs, he’s sharing his expertise on the lecture circuit, speaking at veterinary conferences and seminars across the globe.

### Comprehensive Cancer Care Services

We provide a full range of cancer diagnostics and treatments, including:

  * Advanced imaging and diagnostics

  * Surgical tumor removal

  * Chemotherapy and targeted therapies

  * Pain and symptom management

  * Long-term monitoring and support

 

Every treatment plan is tailored to your pet’s specific condition, focused on both longevity and quality of life.

### Why Choose West Flamingo Animal Hospital?

  * Access to world-class veterinary oncology expertise

  * Compassionate, personalized care for your pet and peace of mind for you

  * A team committed to supporting your pet’s health at every stage

 

### Helping Pets Fight Cancer with Confidence

At West Flamingo Animal Hospital, we’re more than just a veterinary clinic—we’re a trusted partner in your pet’s cancer journey. With Dr. Macy at the helm, you can feel confident that your pet is receiving the best possible care.

# Oncology

We know it can be difficult to discover that your pet has cancer. We’re here to help you every step of the way from diagnosis to treatment.

Image: Golden retriever dog laying down

### Overview

We know it can be extremely difficult to discover that your pet has cancer. We’re here to help you every step of the way from diagnosis to treatment.

We offer a range of treatment plans and tailor them to the needs of your pet in an effort to attack the disease they are fighting and maintain their lifestyle.

### Why would my pet need oncology treatments?

If your pet has been diagnosed with cancer, our team can help you decide on the best treatment plan. Depending on the specific type of cancer your pet has, treatment may include in the following (either stand alone or a combination of treatments):

>   * Radiation therapy

  * Chemotherapy

  * Nutrition/Diet

> ### When should my pet have oncology treatments?

We will determine the proper veterinary treatment schedule based off of your pet’s condition. A diet can be extremely beneficial for patients who are undergoing surgery, radiation, or chemotherapy.

It is important to understand that these treatment options do not necessarily cure your pet’s condition. Treatment options are performed to attack and fight off the effects of your pet’s condition so that they can maintain their quality of life. Many pets who undergo these treatment options have gained months, and sometimes even years of life.

Advanced Care

# Chemotherapy

BBVH assists cancer patients from all over Northern Nevada and Northern California. Sadly, our pets develop many of the same types of cancer that people get. In the past, cancer was a certain death sentence for animals, but today there are a variety of cancers and tumors that can be successfully treated.
Advances in the knowledge of tumor biology, nutrition, surgery, and chemotherapeutic agents have provided options for cancer treatment like never before.
Early Detection of Cancer in Pets is Critical
Early detection and treatment are very important in the successful management of tumors in pets. Routine examinations are recommended for any animal, especially those over 8 years of age, and for certain breeds of dogs (golden retrievers, boxers) that have a relatively higher risk of developing certain types of cancer. In addition, BBVH is one of the few hospitals in Nevada that offers the new therapy for malignant melanomas, a devastating diagnosis.

#### Advanced Oncology Care at Majestic Park Animal Hospital

At Majestic Park Animal Hospital, we’re dedicated to delivering comprehensive, compassionate care for pets facing cancer. Our oncology team provides customized treatment plans, precise staging, and advanced diagnostics—including in-house CT imaging—to ensure every patient receives the individualized attention and care they deserve.

We take a holistic approach to cancer care, integrating innovative therapies with proven medical practices. Our focus extends beyond the disease itself—prioritizing your pet’s comfort, well-being, and quality of life every step of the way.

Our oncology service, led by Dr. David Espinosa, is supported by a highly trained team equipped with state-of-the-art diagnostic tools and the latest chemotherapy and immunotherapy protocols. With extensive experience in diagnosing and managing a wide range of cancers, our team provides expert, compassionate care for every patients.

We offer a full spectrum of cancer care designed to support your pet’s health and comfort:

  * Chemotherapy
  * Immunotherapy (Cancer Vaccines)
  * Surgical Consultation for Tumor Removal
  * Custom Treatment Plans Focused on Quality of Life
  * Access to Emerging Clinical Trials
  * Palliative & Pain Management Care
  * Radiation Therapy Consultation

At Majestic Park Animal Hospital, we combine expertise, innovation, and genuine compassion to deliver advanced cancer care for pets throughout Las Vegas.

Contact us today to schedule an oncology consultation or learn more about how we can help your pet on their journey to healing and comfort.

# Radiation Oncology

Veterinary radiation oncology is a specialized type of cancer treatment that involves radiation to control or remove your pet's tumors and other cancerous growths.

Our veterinary radiation oncologists cantreat both external tumors and internal masses. Tumors that have been unresponsive to other procedures or that can't be surgically removed may also respond well to radiation oncology. Radiation treatment is often just one part of a larger cancer care plan. It may be utilized in conjunction with surgery, chemotherapy, or other treatment methods.We are fully equipped with the most advanced radiation technology available and our veterinary radiation oncologists are highly-trained specialists with many years of experience in treating animals.

We have veterinary oncologists who are experts at diagnosing and treating cancer because that is their sole focus. Our service tailors the treatment protocol for your pet's specific cancer and potential concurrent medical conditions to optimize the outcome and minimize side effects. In addition, our facility has a team of specialists who can assist in the treatment and care of your pet. We want your pet to not just live as long as possible, but to live well. Our Medical Oncology department offers expertise and compassion in treating your pet's cancer. For further information, please telephone us at 505 296-2982 or email us at [email protected].

### My Pet Has Cancer. Now What?

Cancer does appear to be becoming more common in pets, most likely because they are simply living longer. The most important point to realize about this dreaded disease, however, is that just as in people, many forms of the disease can be easily treated, managed, and even cured. Early detection and specialized care are leading to increased survival and cure rates in almost all the types of cancers that afflict pets. From surgery to chemotherapy to radiation therapy, veterinary cancer specialists can offer your pet the very latest diagnostic and treatment options and the best chance of survival. With optimal treatment, cancer in many cases simply becomes another manageable chronic disease.

### Will My Regular Veterinarian Still Be Involved?

In most cases, your regular veterinarian will still supervise your pet's veterinary care and will work in tandem with the veterinary oncologist, veterinary radiation oncologist, and any other members of your pet's veterinary health care team.

### Did You Know?

Dogs and cats have higher age adjusted incidence rates for many kinds of cancers than do humans. For example, dogs are 35 times more likely to get skin cancer than are humans. They suffer from 8 times the amount of bone cancer and 4 times the amount of breast cancer. However, humans are more likely to get lung and stomach cancers than pets.
